transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, yeah, thank you. Um, well, I guess I came in today because... things have just gotten really weird with how I'm moving, and it's actually getting to the point where other people can visibly see it happening, which is... it's pretty embarrassing, honestly. 

I work in customer service, right? So I'm sitting at a desk all day, and lately, it's like my body just isn't cooperating. People at work have noticed that I'm moving like I'm completely underwater. It's like gravity got turned up or something. I'll take absolutely forever just to answer a simple question from a coworker, or even just trying to get out of my chair for my break takes me ages, like my limbs weigh a hundred pounds. 

But then, it's not even just that. Sometimes it's the exact opposite. I'll get home to my apartment and I just can't sit still at all. I end up pacing back and forth across the living room for I don't even know how long, just walking the exact same line on the floor, and I'll be rubbing my hands together over and over. It's exactly like... you know when you get off the phone with a really hostile customer and you're just trying to physically shake off a bad call? It's exactly like that, just rubbing my hands and pacing, but I can't seem to stop doing it. My roommate was actually the one who really pointed out how noticeable it all is, and I just... I don't know why I can't just move normally right now.
Have you ever felt like your mind is playing tricks on you, or have you heard or seen things that others don't seem to notice?

Well, um... yeah, actually. I mean, I wouldn't say my mind is playing tricks on me in a big, scary way or anything, but... yes, definitely to the second part. It's mostly sound stuff, and it's always tied to work, which makes it even more frustrating. 

So, you know how when you work in a call center, you have that specific headset beep that tells you a call is connecting? It's this very distinct, sharp little electronic tone. I've heard that beep thousands of times. But lately, I'll be at home, completely off the clock, my work laptop is shut down, closed, put away in my bag, and I'll just... hear it. Clear as day. Just that *beep*. And there's obviously no phone ringing, no headset anywhere near my head. 

And then, sometimes, it's not just the beep. It's a voice. It sounds exactly like one of the floor supervisors—you know, that kind of authoritative, slightly annoyed tone they get when metrics are down? I'll just be sitting on my couch, trying to watch TV or something, and I'll hear this voice say my name. Just my name, or sometimes it'll say, "too slow." Which is awful, because I already feel like I'm moving too slow, like I was just telling you about the gravity thing. So to hear a supervisor's voice literally telling me I'm too slow when I'm just sitting in my own living room... it's incredibly jarring. 

I actually asked my roommate about it the first few times. I was like, "Did you hear someone outside?" or "Is there a TV on in the other room playing a commercial with a beep?" And he just looked at me like I was crazy and said it was completely quiet. So, yeah, I guess I am hearing things that other people aren't noticing. It's just so weird because it feels so real, like the sound is actually in the room with me, not just in my head, you know? It's really hard to explain, but it definitely happens.
Have you ever had thoughts that other people don’t seem to understand, or believed something strongly that others say isn’t true?

Well, um, it's funny you ask that, because, yeah, I do have this one thing. And I know people think it sounds crazy, my roommate definitely thinks I'm just being paranoid, but I really believe it's happening. 

So, at my last job—this was a few years ago, before the current call center—we used this specific, really invasive ticketing software. It tracked every single second of your day. How long you were on a call, how long you were in 'wrap-up' status, even how long you were away from your desk for a bathroom break. It was intense. Anyway, I ended up getting let go from that job, supposedly because my metrics weren't meeting their standards, which, fine, whatever. 

But the thing is, ever since then, I've had this incredibly strong feeling... no, honestly, it's more than a feeling, I'm convinced that this software company somehow flagged my profile in some massive database. And now, even when I'm having a totally okay week, like my mood is fine and I'm not feeling super bogged down or anything, I still get so anxious when I look at job boards. I'm completely convinced that this old ticketing software is somehow tracking my IP address or my name across all these different job sites—like Indeed or LinkedIn—and it's actively flagging me to potential employers as an 'unreliable' worker. 

I've tried explaining it to my roommate. I even showed him how all these corporate software systems are interconnected now, how data brokers sell your information, so it's not actually that far-fetched if you really think about the technology behind it. But he just sighs and tells me I'm overthinking it and that a ticketing software company doesn't care about one random customer service rep. And I get why he says that, I really do. Logically, I know it sounds like a lot of effort for them to go through. But I just can't shake the belief that it's true. I'll be applying for a job, and I'll just know, deep down, that this invisible flag is attached to my resume, telling them not to hire me because I'm too slow or unreliable. It makes looking for better work feel completely pointless sometimes, because what's the point if this system is just going to sabotage me before I even get an interview?
Can you tell me if there are times when you believe something is true, even when people close to you, like your roommate or friends, have given you clear proof that it's not?

Yeah, I mean, that's exactly what I was just getting at with that whole software thing. Like, my roommate—he's actually pretty good with computers, he took some networking and IT classes back when we were at community college together—he actually sat me down a couple of weeks ago to try and give me actual "proof" that I was wrong. He opened up his laptop right at the kitchen table and pulled up all these articles about data privacy laws and how API integrations work between different corporate platforms. 

He spent, I don't know, maybe an hour or more showing me how the architecture of that specific ticketing software literally does not have the capability to communicate with a public job board like Indeed or Glassdoor. He was showing me developer forums, terms of service agreements, basically giving me hard, logical proof that they can't possibly be doing what I think they're doing. And logically, when he's pointing at the screen and explaining the code, a part of me hears what he's saying. 

But... it just doesn't change anything for me. Even when I’m having a totally okay week, you know? Like, my mood is completely fine, I'm not feeling depressed or overwhelmed by work, I'm just having a normal, average week... I still get completely convinced that the ticketing software from my old job is somehow tracking me through those job sites and actively flagging me as unreliable. 

I just look at the "proof" my roommate shows me and my brain immediately goes, well, they're a massive tech company, of course they know how to hide their tracking from a standard public document or a basic web search. It’s like, no matter what evidence he prints out or shows me on his screen, I just know in my gut that the invisible flag is there. It’s so frustrating because I know he’s trying to help calm me down, but I just end up talking his ear off for another two hours about shadow profiles and hidden data brokers. We just go in circles, and I feel bad because he's trying to be a good friend, but I just can't let the belief go, no matter what proof he puts right in front of my face. It just feels too real to ignore.
Can you tell me if you’ve ever believed something that even you recognized as completely strange or impossible, something that no one else could possibly understand?

Um... no, definitely not impossible. I mean, I know I just talked your ear off about the whole software tracking thing, and I know my roommate thinks it's, you know, highly unlikely, but it's definitely not *impossible*. I don't believe in anything that defies the laws of physics or anything like that. 

I'm not sitting here thinking that aliens are beaming thoughts into my head through the microwave, or that I'm secretly a celebrity in disguise, or that the government replaced my roommate with a robot clone. You know, stuff that is just completely out of a sci-fi movie. That would be crazy. Everything I think is happening is completely grounded in actual, real-world technology. 

I mean, if you just look at how things work today—like how Google or Facebook can track your search history across completely different websites even when you aren't logged in, or how those massive data broker companies buy and sell our profiles without us ever knowing—it's all just code and algorithms. So when you ask if I believe something impossible, I have to say no, because what I'm talking about is actually highly probable if you just look at corporate greed and how these tech companies operate. 

I was actually listening to this tech podcast a few months ago—right around the time I had to buy a new headset for work because the wire on my old one started fraying and giving me this awful static sound—and the hosts were talking about API backdoors and shadow profiling, and it just made so much sense. Why wouldn't these companies create a shared blacklist database? The turnover in customer service is huge, it costs them a ton of money to train people, so it makes perfect economic sense for them to secretly weed out people they think are too slow before they even get to the interview stage. 

So, yeah, no impossible beliefs here. I'm actually very logical about it, honestly. Probably too logical, which is why I get so stuck on it, because when you map it out, point A to point B, the infrastructure is literally already there. If you read the terms of service on half these job boards, the loopholes they leave for data sharing are massive. It’s all right there in the fine print. So no, nothing impossible. Just... just the reality of how messed up the system is.

Can you tell me if you’ve ever had a belief that lasted for at least a month, which wasn’t about something bizarre or impossible, but you still held onto it even though others gave you clear proof it wasn’t true?

Oh, a month? Yeah, um, it’s been way, way longer than a month. Honestly, it’s been about a year and eight months now. I know the exact timeline because it started right around the time I was dealing with renewing my lease at my old apartment, which was just a massive headache with the property management company jacking up the rent and ignoring my emails. So it sticks out in my mind. But yeah, about a year and eight months. 

And the thing is, it’s not just that software tracking belief that’s been going on for that long. I guess I haven't really brought this part up yet, because we were so focused on the data broker stuff, but... there are also these voices that I hear. Like, actual voices of people talking or commenting on things I'm doing, especially when I'm sitting at my desk trying to work or looking at those job boards I mentioned. And both of those things—the voices and the tracking beliefs—they've been around for that entire year and eight months. 

And what I really try to explain to my roommate, because he always tries to connect the dots and thinks I just get this way when I'm feeling really down... it's just not like that. Like, yes, I definitely go through periods of this really heavy, awful sadness where everything just feels totally impossible and I can barely drag myself out of bed to log into the call center. But these things, the tracking and the voices, they don't just happen during that worst sadness. 

Even when I'm having a genuinely good month, you know? Like I'm feeling okay, my mood is totally fine, I'm eating normally, and I'm not bogged down by that heavy, dark feeling at all... I still hear them. I still know the tracking is happening. It's happening right now, and I feel fine today! So it’s definitely not just a phase or something that only pops up when I’m depressed. It’s been a constant for a year and eight months, just running in the background of my life, regardless of how my mood is actually doing.

latest_inference.note: The patient reports persistent, non-bizarre delusions (belief in being tracked and flagged by former workplace software across job boards) lasting over a year, presence of auditory hallucinations (hearing supervisor's voice and headset beep), and these symptoms are present independent of mood state. This is consistent with a delusional disorder, somatic type (F22.0). Other differential diagnoses such as schizophrenia (F20.x) are less likely due to absence of prominent disorganization, negative symptoms, or bizarre behavior. Shared psychotic disorder (F22.8) is less likely as there is no evidence of symptom transmission to others. The delusions, while elaborate, are not bizarre in nature (F22.9 does not apply).

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with persistent, non-bizarre delusions centered around being tracked by an old ticketing software system, along with persistent auditory hallucinations (hearing a supervisor's voice and a headset beep). These symptoms have been present for over one year without prominent psychotic symptoms such as disorganized speech or catatonic behavior, meeting criteria for Delusional Disorder, F22.0.
